actualPattern: ^Error: literal `[^`]*` is empty; a literal must match at least one character$
reason: A pattern that can't be constructed is GrammarError::Pattern in cpat-rs's own words, which name the pattern; v12 passes on its Literal constructor's text.
cites: DESIGN.md §18, deviations: "A pattern that can't be constructed (an empty literal, …) is GrammarError::Pattern with cpat-rs's own message"

reason: v12 looks a pattern's custom tokens up in a plain object (`customTokensMap[pattern.name] ?? []`), so a pattern named `constructor` (a literal in the TypeScript and saya grammars) finds Object.prototype.constructor and AutoComplete throws. cpat-rs keeps custom tokens in a map and suggests normally.
cites: DESIGN.md §23, "v12 bugs the harness found": custom tokens by a prototype key

expected: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
reason: Input nested past Limits::max_depth (1024 frames) halts the parse with too_deep, where v12 recurses until the JS engine overflows its stack (jq's 3000-deep paren bomb).
cites: DESIGN.md §11, deviations: "Input nested past `Limits::max_depth` halts with `too_deep`; v12 recurses until the JS engine throws `RangeError`"

expected: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'firstIndex')
reason: v12's FiniteRepeat with a trimmed divider takes "no items" for "ended on a divider" (0 % 2 === 0) when its first item fails, pops a node that isn't there and throws. cpat-rs reports the failed repeat and the choice tries its next alternative.
cites: DESIGN.md §23, "v12 bugs the harness found": a trimmed bounded repeat whose first item fails

reason: A sequence that runs out of text records its error's last index past the text's end. v12 spells that as its cursor's index + 1, and its cursor sits on the start of the last grapheme, so when that grapheme is wider than one UTF-16 unit (an emoji, CRLF, a letter and a combining mark) v12's number is inside it; cpat-rs's `last` is the text's length. AutoComplete's errorAtIndex is read off that error. The same position, written two ways; text whose last grapheme is one unit wide gives the same number in both.
cites: DESIGN.md §11, deviations: "A `Sequence` that runs out of text records its error's `last` at the end of the text"; §23

reason: A literal `(` matches the base of the grapheme `(` + mark, and the next pattern starts after the whole grapheme, so the mark belongs to no node. v12's Expression then normalizes its node's ranges from the joined values (`node.normalize`), which moves them back over the skipped unit, and moves the cursor to the shifted end: what follows the expression is parsed from inside it, the `]` is missed and the whole parse fails (error from 0). cpat-rs keeps the ranges the text gives, so its parse ends at the `]` and only the skipped mark is unmatched (error from the value's length).
cites: DESIGN.md §12, deviations: "an expression's ranges are not normalized over a skipped part of a grapheme"; §23

reason: v12 starts the error after a partial match at the matched value's length, a count of UTF-16 units used as a position. When the value skipped part of a grapheme (a literal matched the base of the base + skin-tone modifier, `~` of `~🏽` or `a` of `a🏽`), that count can land between the two halves of a surrogate pair, which no byte offset names; cpat-rs reports the pair's start, one unit earlier. The furthest error is that same error.
cites: DESIGN.md §5, "exec matches as v12 does" (the summary error's start); §23

reason: A Pratt operator literal (`-`, `+`, `~`) matches the base of a grapheme it starts and a joiner (combining mark, skin-tone modifier, ZWJ, variation selector) is skipped. v12's Expression normalizes its node's ranges from the joined values, and the leaf nodes it moves are the same objects the cursor recorded as matches, so the furthest leaf's end moves back over the skipped units after the fact. AutoComplete places its options (and its errorAtIndex) at that moved end and trims by the moved slice, and generateErrorMessage counts its column to it. cpat-rs keeps the ranges the text gives: the options sit where the text ends.
cites: DESIGN.md §12, deviations: "an expression's ranges are not normalized over a skipped part of a grapheme"; §23
